The papersThe code

Pathway activity from condition-responsive genes, dug back up.

53 results: 4 exact, 18 agree, 23 partly agree, 6 differ, 2 not attempted. The lost method was rebuilt from the paper's Methods, and the seven datasets from GEO, Bioconductor and the GSEA site.

Fig. 2. Mean |t| of the top 1% to 10% pathway markers (PAC, PAC_all), their CORGs and as many top genes, in the dataset the markers come from (A, C, E, G) and in the other cohort (B, D, F, H). Ours drawn in the published colours.

The breast datasets' preprocessing and probe-to-gene mapping are not stated, and our breast data are not the paper's: only 3 of Table S2's 15 CORG lists come back. The source curves (A, C) keep the published shape and order; the verification curves (B, D) differ by up to 1.0. One point is off: PAC_all at 2% reads 2.43 on the figure and 2.55 in our run; the other 19 are within 0.1. One point is off: PAC at 2% reads 1.73 on the figure and 1.37 in our run (the paper's curve rises at 2% and falls again); every other readable point is within 0.1. Boston's top pathways are not those of Tian's statistic on the GSEA Boston file: Table 1's Boston-to-Michigan pathways rank as low as 375th in it. The Boston CORGs themselves are exact (Table 1), so the difference is in which pathways are ranked; our PAC is up to 0.43 above the figure in G and up to 0.54 below it in H.

23 of 42 bars within 0.02. PAC_random differs because the paper's random sets skip the CORG search (supported); NF-kB is near 1 for every method in our data (open); the rest differ by up to 0.07 with unstated classifier settings. 5 of 8 bars within 0.02. Boston to Michigan: our PAC is 0.56 against 0.66; the paper's Boston markers were not Tian's top 52 (a sensitivity run without the pre-selection gives PAC 0.71); the Gene bars of both lung directions are 0.02 to 0.03 high. -log10 p of a Wilcoxon test on 500 paired AUCs moves with every unstated setting and with the random partitions; no printed value comes back to its decimal. Where both are significant the sizes are close (Breast Netherlands 19.2 against 16.9); the significance pattern is compared in text.pac_beats_gene_within and _across.

Fig. S4

Fig. S4. As Fig. 4 for the Table S2 pathways in the two breast datasets, metastatic patients first; its cells are too narrow to read one by one, so each class is ordered by its patients' mean activity and only each row's direction is scored.

Partly agrees
Fig. S4, each pathway's activity higher or lower in metastasis (breast)
25 of 26 values, Partly agrees

25 of 26 rows go the same way as the published heatmaps. The miss is KRAS up-regulated genes in Breast USA: the heatmap uses each dataset's own CORGs, and ours for this set (COL4A1 TUFT1 TGFBI) are not the paper's (TUFT1 P4HA2 COL4A1), because our USA data are not the authors'.

Fig. S5, CORGs per pathway in the top 10%

The box plots summarize the CORG counts of each dataset's top 52 pathways; the medians come back in 5 of 7 datasets. Which 52 pathways the paper counted is not certain (Boston's differ, fig2.g), and the breast data differ.

Every result

Every figure, table and claim of the paper. Figure values are read off the published figures (Figs 2 and 3) or the vector supplements (Figs S1 to S5); a value agrees within 0.1 |t| (Fig. 2), 0.02 AUC (Figs 3, S2, S3), 0.05 overlap (Fig. S1) or 50 of 500 classifiers (frequencies).

Port against the authors' codeNot attemptedThe authors' software is lost: no link, no availability statement and no code in the supplement; searches of GitHub, CRAN, Bioconductor, PyPI and the authors' lab pages found nothing (issue #47). pacorg is written from the Methods and checked against the paper.
pacorg, the method as a Python packageAgrees

The main claim, that classifiers on CORG-based pathway activity beat classifiers on genes, holds in Breast Netherlands, Lung Michigan, Lung Boston and Michigan to Boston. It does not hold in our NF-kB, Prostate, Breast USA, USA to Netherlands and Boston to Michigan runs: our breast and NF-kB data are not the authors' (open), Boston's pathway pre-selection differs (open), and Prostate's small gap has no tested cause beyond the unstated classifier settings.

The method
CORG search, pathway activity and Tian's pre-selection, as the Python package pacorg.

What stayed buried

  • The breast data as the authors prepared them: 3 of Table S2's 15 CORG lists come back.
  • Boston's top pathways: the paper's are not those of Tian's statistic on the GSEA Boston file.
  • NF-kB: in our 24 arrays every classifier is near perfect; the paper's gene classifier is at 0.82.
  • How the paper computed the CORG overlap of Fig. S1.

The main claim, that classifiers on CORG-based pathway activity beat classifiers on genes, holds in Breast Netherlands, Lung Michigan, Lung Boston and Michigan to Boston. It does not hold in our NF-kB, Prostate, Breast USA, USA to Netherlands and Boston to Michigan runs: our breast and NF-kB data are not the authors' (open), Boston's pathway pre-selection differs (open), and Prostate's small gap has no tested cause beyond the unstated classifier settings.

What we matched

How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.

Activity
Each gene z-scored over all samples; a set's activity is the sum of member z-scores over sqrt(k).
CORGs
Members ranked by t, added while |t| of the activity rises (pooled-variance t).
Pre-selection
Tian's statistic as sum of t over sqrt(members), top 52 of 522; the Methods say average t, but Table 1 and Fig. 2 follow the standardized sum.
Classifier
Logistic regression; markers added in order of p-value, the count chosen by validation AUC; 100 runs of 5-fold CV.
Data
GSEA lung files as distributed; GEO and Bioconductor for the other five, mapped to MSigDB v1.0 symbols through Entrez Gene IDs.

Pathway activity came back exactly where the paper's own data survive: every CORG list of Table 1.
